global_caption: The video contains 5 shots. It is a realistic cool-toned classroom chemistry experiment short film, unfolding in the authentic atmosphere of a real school laboratory. The color palette is consistently cool blue-gray, primarily using natural cool light supplemented by localized side lighting. The emotional tone remains cheerful with a hint of tension.
shot1: Shot 1 opens directly into the frame with a wide eye-level composition showing the classroom lab bench, blackboard in the background, cold daylight from the window, and neatly arranged beakers. A blurred test tube rack in the foreground adds depth. The overall lighting is cool and even.
shot2: Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot to a close-up side view, framing her upper body and hands. Side light slants in from the window, creating cold white highlights on the beaker's edge. The background is softly blurred, preserving the classroom outline. Focus is locked on the pipette in her hand and the other cup containing pale blue reagent. She steadily lifts her hand and drops the transparent liquid one drop at a time into the cup. The camera makes a very controlled micro-following pan, allowing viewers to clearly see the fine ripples before and after the transparent liquid enters the pale blue solution.
shot3: Shot 3 cuts hard via action match to an overhead close-up. The lab bench surface is neatly laid out, with the edges of the vessels forming intersecting circular and diagonal graphic patterns. Shallow depth of field focuses all attention on the internal changes of the liquid. Under cool light, the two liquids rapidly fuse in the container, changing color quickly from light blue to deeper purple. Fine thread-like swirls appear first at the center, followed by gradual thickening, pulling out sticky textures, and forming a translucent gel-like consistency. Surface reflections shift from scattered moving highlights to more continuous moist shine. The camera remains stable in overhead view, making only a minimal push-in to enhance the realism of the material transition.
shot4: Shot 4 transitions smoothly via a lateral dolly move from the lab bench to the window-side record table. In a medium-close eye-level composition, the window frame and table edge form clear horizontal and vertical lines. The background is a softly defocused corner of the classroom. Cold natural light becomes more prominent on her goggles and the beaker surface. She shows a surprised expression, eyes slightly widened, humming lightly while gently swaying the beaker to observe the slow flow of the semi-solid substance inside. The gel-like liquid leaves a viscous trail on the cup wall before slowly retracting, clearly indicating a distinct semi-solid state change. The subtle The camera continues its dolly movement and slightly stabilizes, making the observation motion feel coherent and natural.
shot5: Shot 5 transitions gently via a soft fade-in/fade-out into a near close-up. The camera focuses on her raised hands holding the result and half her smiling face under natural cool light by the window. The composition centers the beaker visually, with sharp foreground and completely softened background. Cold daylight passes through the container, giving the internal substance a sparkling translucent quality. The previously purple gel-like material appears in stillness with a delicate jelly-like coagulated texture, its surface highlight stable and clear, as if frozen in light. She raises the result high and slightly rotates it to confirm the color. Joy overcomes tension, aligning with the freeze-frame presentation of the result. The camera makes one final slow push-in, stopping at the moment the crystalline texture is most vivid, completing the display of the experimental outcome.
